0.evidence_source: Translation and psychometric evaluation of a Standard Chinese version of the Body Appreciation Scale-2
0._section_summary: The section contains the title 'Translation and psychometric evaluation of a Standard Chinese version of the Body Appreciation Scale-2' and the author line 'Viren Swami, Siu-Kuen Ng, David Barrond'. The title indicates this work involves translating and evaluating the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2). No study numbering, sample characteristics, country, data collection method, BMI assessment, or correlation results are provided in the supplied text.

1.evidence_source: The present study examined the factorial and construct validity of a Standard Chinese translation of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS-2; Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b).
1._section_summary: This paper evaluated the factorial and construct validity of a Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2 in a sample of 191 women and 154 men from mainland China who were resident in Hong Kong. Confirmatory factor analysis supported a one-dimensional BAS-2 structure invariant across sex, and body appreciation scores showed good internal consistency and expected correlations with self-esteem and life satisfaction; in women only, scores were significantly correlated with weight discrepancy and BMI. The findings suggest the Standard Chinese BAS-2 is equivalent to the parent scale and useful for cross-cultural research.

2.evidence_source: "In order to facilitate wider use of the BAS-2 in Chinese-speaking populations, we report on the translation and validation of a Standard Chinese version of the scale."
2._section_summary: The introduction reviews prior cross-cultural validations of the BAS and BAS-2, noting two non-US studies (Iran and Hong Kong) that found a one-dimensional BAS-2 structure and sex differences in body appreciation. The paper reports the translation and validation of a Standard Chinese BAS-2, using confirmatory factor analysis to test factorial validity and sex invariance, and examining construct validity via associations with self-esteem, life satisfaction, BMI (women)/BMI^2 (men), and weight discrepancy (women).

3.evidence_source: Body appreciation. Participants completed the 10-item BAS-2 (Tylka & Wood-Barcalow, 2015b; see Appendix for items in English and Standard Chinese).
3._section_summary: This Measures section reports that body appreciation was assessed using the 10-item BAS-2; women's actual-ideal weight discrepancy was measured with the Photographic Figure Rating Scale (PFRS) (men skipped this measure); self-esteem was measured with a 9-item version of the Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale (one item removed) with Cronbach's α = .82 (women) and .83 (men); life satisfaction was measured with the 5-item SWLS with Cronbach's α = .84. The section does not provide sample size, country, recruitment/source, survey method, BMI measurement, or any correlations between body appreciation and BMI, nor does it label any studies (e.g., 'Study 1').

4.evidence_source: "Once ethics approval was obtained, we prepared Standard Chinese translations of the BAS-2..."
4._section_summary: This section describes procedures for a single study conducted between June and December 2015: Standard Chinese translations of the BAS-2, PFRS, and SWLS were prepared via back-translation, and participants (required to be from mainland China and fluent in Standard Chinese) completed anonymous paper-and-pencil questionnaires after providing written consent. The study was advertised on campus locations and questionnaires were completed in private cubicles; no sample size, demographic breakdowns, BMI assessment, or correlation statistics are reported here. There is no mention of 'Study 1' or multiple studies in this section.

5.evidence_source: To determine whether the BAS-2 was invariant across sex, we tested for invariance at the configural (i.e., whether similar factors are measured), factor loading (i.e., whether the magnitude of factor loadings is the same), and intercept (i.e., whether the intercept of the regression relating each item to its factor is the same) level (Chen, 2007).
5._section_summary: This section describes use of confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) to evaluate a single-factor measurement model for the BAS-2 with standard goodness-of-fit indices (chi-square normed, RMSEA, SRMR, CFI). It also reports testing measurement invariance of the BAS-2 across sex and examining sex differences in body appreciation scores, with a comparison to Swami and Ng (2015).

6.evidence_source: "CFA was conducted on the 10 items of the BAS-2, where all items loaded onto a single latent variable."
6._section_summary: This section reports a confirmatory factor analysis of the 10-item BAS-2 in a single sample (N=345), indicating a one-dimensional structure with generally good-to-excellent factor loadings (Items 1 and 9 were fair) and acceptable model fit (CFI = .953, RMSEA = .084, SRMR = .047). Multi-group analyses supported configural and loading invariance across sex and indicated intercept invariance, suggesting the BAS-2 structure is equivalent across male and female sub-samples. The text does not label the analysis as 'Study 1' or mention multiple distinct studies.

7.evidence_source: "We calculated total body appreciation scores by taking the mean of all 10 items." and "We also obtained data from Swami and Ng (2015) of respondents who had completed the Cantonese version of the BAS-2 (women n=457, men n=417)".
7._section_summary: This section reports further analyses of body appreciation (mean of 10 BAS-2 items) from the primary sample (gender comparisons and correlations) and additional analyses using data obtained from Swami & Ng (2015) (Cantonese vs Standard Chinese versions; women n=457, men n=417). It highlights gender-specific correlations between body appreciation and BMI in the primary sample (women r = -0.19; men r = -0.13) and ANCOVA results comparing language versions and sex in the Swami & Ng sample.

8.evidence_source: Using CFA, we found that the one-dimensional model, in which all items loaded onto a single factor, had adequate fit in respondents who completed a Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2.
8._section_summary: The discussion reports that a one-dimensional Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2 showed adequate fit, good internal consistency, and convergent validity; body appreciation correlated with life satisfaction and self-esteem and—specifically in women—with weight discrepancy and BMI. The BAS-2 factor structure was invariant across sex, no significant overall sex difference in BAS-2 scores was found, and Standard Chinese respondents had slightly higher (negligible effect) body appreciation than Cantonese respondents; the section calls for replication in other Standard Chinese samples and additional validity evidence.

9.evidence_source: Discussion: '...the one-dimensional model, in which all items loaded onto a single factor, had adequate fit in respondents who completed a Standard Chinese translation of the BAS-2.'

9._section_summary: The section reports that a one-dimensional model of the Standard Chinese BAS-2 demonstrated adequate fit, internal consistency, and convergent validity. Measurement invariance across sex was supported, and no significant overall difference in BAS-2 scores between women and men was found, though associations with BMI were observed in women only. The authors compare Standard Chinese and Cantonese respondents and note limitations and directions for future validation work.

10._section_summary: The Discussion reports that confirmatory factor analysis supported a one-dimensional factor structure for the Standard Chinese version of the BAS-2 and that this version demonstrated good internal consistency and convergent validity. The factor structure was invariant across sex, there was no significant difference in BAS-2 scores between women and men, and body appreciation was significantly associated with life satisfaction and self-esteem, and with BMI and weight discrepancy in women only; the section also compares Standard Chinese and Cantonese respondent groups (Standard Chinese scores were slightly higher but with a negligible effect size).
